title: Check yourself: Isolation, fallbacks and resuming a run

questions.stem: Scenario: Elm Biotech's plan has five tasks: a, b, c, d and e. Task b breaks for good, d needs b, and c and e need neither. What should the runner report?

options.text: a, c and e done, b failed, d skipped because of b, with each reason stated
options.says: Only the task that needed b is affected, and the report lists what is done, what failed and what was skipped.

options.text: The whole run counts as failed, since one broken part makes the rest untrustworthy for the reader
options.says: Ruled out because the failure is isolated: "it ends only its own branch".

options.text: Task a done, with the later tasks left unreported until someone has repaired the broken one
options.says: Ruled out because the report names "what is done, what failed and why, and what was skipped because of it", and silence about d hides a gap.

options.text: Five tasks done, with d computed from a plausible guess at what b would have returned
options.says: Ruled out because a task whose input failed is skipped "with a reason that names the failed one", and is not fed a guess.

origin.section: A failure stays in its branch

questions.stem: Scenario: Rowan Insights' search agent fails, and a cheaper backup agent answers the task. The runner keeps the backup's answer. What should it do with that result?

options.text: Write it to the store of finished work, so that a later run does not repeat the same effort
options.says: Ruled out because a stored answer makes the task look done: "the weaker answer would become permanent by accident".

options.text: Use it, flag it as degraded, and leave it out of the store of finished work
options.says: A degraded result is used and flagged, and it is not stored, so a later run can try the primary again.

options.text: Discard it, because only the primary agent's answers may ever appear in a final report
options.says: Ruled out because the fallback "keeps the run moving", and discarding it loses the point of having one.

options.text: Use it and say nothing, because the reader of the report wants only the content of the answer
options.says: Ruled out because the task is listed as degraded "so that the report and the caller know the answer is weaker than planned".

origin.section: A fallback degrades, and says so
